name: Fiorella
description: Marc Vetri's tiny pasta bar tucked into a former butcher shop turns out a short, ever-changing menu of fresh handmade pastas. Seats are scarce and the vibe is intimate, making it one of the neighborhood's most coveted reservations.

name: Ralph's Italian Restaurant
description: Open since 1900, Ralph's is a red-sauce institution that has fed everyone from Frank Sinatra to sitting presidents. Generous plates of old-school Italian-American classics come with the warm, time-capsule dining room that defines the block.

name: Dante & Luigi's
description: One of the country's oldest continuously operating Italian restaurants, Dante & Luigi's has anchored the corner of 10th and Catharine since 1899. Career waiters and a menu of handmade pastas and hearty gravy dishes keep the old-world tradition intact.

name: Villa di Roma
description: Right in the heart of the 9th Street market, this family-run holdover serves the kind of no-frills South Philly red-sauce cooking that locals grew up on. Expect big portions, a bustling bar, and an unpretentious feel.

name: Saloon
description: A clubby, dimly lit destination for special occasions, Saloon pairs prime steaks and chops with a deep Italian menu and a serious wine list. It has been one of the neighborhood's splurge spots for decades.

name: Mawn
description: This acclaimed BYOB noodle house channels Cambodian and broader Southeast Asian flavors into a tight, produce-driven menu. The crab-fat noodles, roti canai, and whole fish have made it one of the hardest tables to land in South Philly.

name: Casa Mexico
description: From James Beard-winning chef Cristina Martinez, Casa Mexico delivers deeply flavored, regionally authentic Mexican cooking a few doors from her legendary South Philly Barbacoa. The citrus-and-chile marinated pibil pork is a standout.

name: Blue Corn
description: A full-service Mexican restaurant and bar known for handmade blue corn tortillas and a wide menu spanning ceviche, huaraches, and tortas. The al pastor tacos with pineapple and Oaxaca cheese are the crowd favorite.

name: Angelo's Pizzeria
description: Locals line up for Angelo's Sicilian and round pies, hoagies, and one of the city's most praised cheesesteaks on a fresh-baked roll. It's cash-only and worth the wait that regularly stretches down 9th Street.

name: Alma del Mar
description: This bright seafood and brunch spot, featured on Netflix's Queer Eye, leans on fresh fish and Latin-inflected plates. Its lobster Benedict, piled with meat over a poached egg and hollandaise, is the reason weekend crowds gather.
